name: Bounds Tree Intersection Push Pruning

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: gpux BoundsTree slow search with apps/test_suite wide DataTable headed WebGPU
hypothesisMarkdown:
# Hypothesis

Testing child bounds before pushing them onto `BoundsTree::search_stack` will eliminate stack writes and later pop/branch work for spatially irrelevant nodes in the measured slow-search path. Because the current algorithm already performs the same intersection test immediately after pop, moving it to the parent expansion boundary preserves maximum-order results and tree shape while reducing the wide DataTable's 25,720 visited-node count and not regressing headed WebGPU latency.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
# Measurement plan

1. In `find_max_ordering`, reject a non-intersecting root before pushing it, and push internal children only when both `max_order > max_found` and their bounds intersect the query. Remove the now-redundant post-pop spatial test; do not change max-order pruning, child order, insertion, or tree shape.
2. Update the focused diagnostic assertion for the exact root-rejection visit count. Preserve the existing 1,000-seed brute-force ordering oracle.
3. Run diagnostics-off/on compilation, focused bounds-tree tests, Clippy, nested formatting, and two serialized headed WebGPU candidate processes at DPR 1 and 2.
4. Accept only if the warmed search-node visit count drops at both DPRs, renderer/scroll contracts remain exact, and product p95 does not materially regress. Otherwise revert to the checkpoint and record failure.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
# Expected outcome

The wide DataTable retains 504 insertions, seven max-leaf hits, 495 slow searches, 14,351 insertion child evaluations, 576 retained nodes, nine batches, 12 queue writes, 10 bind groups, two passes, and zero terminal error, while search-node visits fall below the 25,720 checkpoint count. The direct stack-operation reduction should preserve or improve paced p95 at both DPRs across two candidate processes.

playwright: Two independent wide DataTable candidate processes passed 4/4 headed Chromium WebGPU projects across DPR 1 and DPR 2.
Every candidate reported 4,440 search-node visits and unchanged tree, renderer, and scroll-correctness counters.
rayx: All runtime proof used apps/test_suite; apps/lab was neither launched nor modified.
Diagnostics-off/on gpux checks, wasm32 gpui_web diagnostics check, the 1,000-seed randomized ordering oracle, Clippy with warnings denied, and nested formatting passed.
counters: Moving intersection rejection before stack push reduced warmed search-node visits by 21,280 per frame, from 25,720 to 4,440 (82.74%).
Candidate median paced p95 was 26.91 ms at DPR 1 and 27.04 ms at DPR 2 versus checkpoint 26.76/28.05 ms.

All four projects retained 504 insertions, seven max-leaf hits, 495 slow searches, 14,351 insertion child evaluations, 576 nodes, nine batches, 12 writes, 10 bind groups, two passes, and zero terminal error.

reportMarkdown:
# Bounds tree intersection push-pruning report

`BoundsTree::find_max_ordering` now rejects a non-intersecting root before stacking and filters non-intersecting children at internal-node expansion. The old algorithm performed the identical bounds test only after popping each node, so the change removes unnecessary `NonNull` stack writes, pops, and post-pop branches without changing max-order pruning, child order, insertion, tree shape, or assigned draw orders.

The warmed wide DataTable search-node count fell from 25,720 to 4,440 at both DPRs, eliminating 21,280 visits (82.74%) per frame. Two independent headed Test Suite processes passed all four DPR projects. Every other tree and renderer counter stayed exact: 504 insertions, seven max-leaf hits, 495 slow searches, 14,351 insertion child evaluations, 576 retained nodes, nine batches, 12 writes, 10 bind groups, two passes, zero atlas writes/restarts, one submission, and zero terminal scroll error.

Candidate median paced p95 was 26.91 ms at DPR 1, 0.56% above the single checkpoint process, and 27.04 ms at DPR 2, 3.60% below it. Throughput remained process-noisy, so acceptance rests on the exact stack-operation reduction, randomized semantic oracle, and non-regressing p95 rather than a claimed end-to-end speedup. Diagnostics-off/on gpux checks, wasm32 gpui_web diagnostics check, the 1,000-seed randomized bounds-tree test, Clippy with warnings denied, and nested formatting all passed.
decisionMarkdown:
# Decision

Accept. The change performs the same spatial test earlier and demonstrably removes 82.74% of search-stack visits in the profiled workload without adding state, changing tree structure, or regressing product p95. Do not combine this with child ordering or insertion-descent changes; those require separate hypotheses.
